TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Banda Sea, southern approaches
DATE 25 November 2028 · 0540 local
SIDE Royal Australian Navy
WINDOW 75 min, closes at 112
Collins class submarine. Photo: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Leonard... · Public domain · cropped
"Under pressure, you don't rise to the occasion - you sink to the level of your training."
- military training maxim, speaker unknown; often called a SEAL saying

BANDA SEA, before dawn. STUART has one shaft, thirty-one wounded and a six-knot engineering limit. Bring her south-south-east to Darwin's tug handover line. The recovery remains the main task; sinking the opposing ships is not a substitute for a live frigate at the line.

SCREEN AND SEARCH: A Kilo is working the south-western approach. Flying Shark 31 and 32 are already committed and join from the north at minute five. Keep the helicopter or an escort ahead of Stuart while the air-defence ship covers the straggler. HMAS SHEEAN is allocated on the eastern barrier, submerged with weapons held. You command her; deconflict her patrol from the flight's torpedo attacks. She is a theatre attachment for this operation, not a new permanent roster purchase.

BREAK THE RELAY: An armed Okean trawler, operating as BANDA SURVEYOR, is east of the recovery lane. She is due to release a fast missile craft at minute twenty-five. Identify the contact among the civilian traffic. If you destroy this hostile relay before that deadline, the follow-on craft never joins. Once released, sinking the relay will not recall it. The first air raid and Kilo are independent. Continue searching for the other threats with your own sensors.

CHOICES AND CONSEQUENCES: Split the screen to hunt the relay and risk the southern submarine approach, or keep the escorts close and prepare for the later surface attack. Classifying the relay, silencing it, neutralizing the Kilo and preserving Sheean earn separate credit. They are optional; the main recovery ends the mission, so do them before Stuart reaches the line if you choose. MT BANDA SPIRIT and MV TANIMBAR TRADER remain neutral throughout. Harming either fails the operation.
CHIEF MASON has taped a red spider over the broken shaft repeater. Mercer says the spider is the only member of this detachment authorized to move faster than six knots.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.
Commodore Alex Mercer
COMMANDER'S INTENT

Bring Stuart to the line at six knots. Assign separate ASW and air-defence sectors. Use Sheean without confusing her with TANGO. Break the eastern relay before minute 25 if the screen can spare the effort; otherwise meet the fast craft without abandoning the wounded or firing on a merchant.
• Bring STUART to the line
• Harm no neutral shipping
• Classify the armed relay trawler
• Silence the armed relay trawler
• Neutralize the Kilo on the recovery approach
• Preserve SHEEAN

Your recovery detachment and Stuart; Sheean on an independent eastern submarine barrier, weapons held. Two protected neutral merchants. Opposing: one Kilo, a J-15D strike pair at minute five, one armed relay trawler and one fast missile craft at minute twenty-five if the relay survives its deadline.

The planned window is 75 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 37 minutes more; the operation is closed at 112 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
